overview: Euclid DR1 dominated the period: a pipeline combining neural-network classification, citizen science and expert grading released 15,072 strong-lens candidates. Other work released benchmarks and tools — the FAIR Universe weak-lensing uncertainty challenge, differentiable JAX/PyTorch galpy backends, LLM-extracted dark-matter model and galaxy-discussion catalogues — alongside neural posterior estimation for gravitational-wave tests of general relativity.
themes: ML for gravitational-wave detection and parameter estimation
LLM and foundation-model tools for literature mining and interpretability
benchmarks for cosmological inference and uncertainty quantification
